newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Government okays sale of Colombia's Concasa.
newsitem.headline: Government okays sale of Colombia's Concasa.

text.p: The government has given its final approval to the sale of a controlling stake in Concasa, a savings and loan owned by Colombia's National Coffee Fund, the financial daily La Republica said Thursday.

It said a minimum price of just over $110 million had been set for the 61.33 share of Concasa currently in the hands of the Coffee Fund and Bancafe, a bank administered like the Fund by the National Coffee Growers' Association.
According to La Republica, the Finance Ministry authorized the sale of Concasa in a decree issued Monday. Ministry spokesmen could not be reached for immediate comment.

The ministry ordered the state privatization committee, Fogafin, to arrange the sale of the controlling stake in Concasa on Colombia's thee stock exchanges by no later than June 30 of next year, La Republica said.

Recent press reports have said the Coffee Fund, which guarantees the purchase of crops from growers and has provided industry-wide stability for decades, was saddled with a debt of more than $800 million. But Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo denied this in remarks to reporters earlier this month, saying the fund was expected to end the year with a deficit of no more than $159 million. -- Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
